ac975a5fdc56.text: Went to a guy's house to check his smoke detectors. He'd already taken them all down and laid them on the kitchen table like they were under arrest. Nine of them. He'd been waiting. Said he'd been waiting since Tuesday. I put new batteries in, he followed me room to room asking if that beep was normal. Sir, that is the beep working.

bb1dd8b8de6a.text: I went on a field visit and the whole thing was just holding a clipboard while a woman explained her pantry. She pointed at a can of condensed milk like it was evidence. I wrote "condensed milk" down real serious. That's my job now, transcribing pantries. Six years of school to nod slowly at soup.

7d0931e374b3.text: Putting away groceries as a spider. You put them away once, you got eight legs, you're done in nine seconds. My wife comes in, she's like, "You already? I just went to the bathroom." Yeah, Diane, I did the whole kitchen, I also rebuilt the web in the corner. It's structural now. Don't hang your purse on it.

e4844028a13b.text: Everyone asks Anansi where the stories come from. Same place the webs come from, friend. My backside. I'm spinning it out of my own body and giving it to you for nothing. But go ahead, pay the exterminator eighteen hundred dollars to kill the one tenant who eats all your mosquitoes.

3a786896bc23.text: I do Cosmic Reiki, which is just Reiki but I hum in a frequency your doctor can't hear. Last week I healed a guy's bad knee and he still sent me a co-pay. I opened a portal to the fifth dimension and the dude asked if that was covered by insurance. Sir, I just moved your chakras with light I grew myself.

5a9cd8518da9.text: I'm a being of light, so every morning I have to choose my own solidity. Humans wake up stuck with whatever body showed up, I get options and still pick a boring one. I tell myself this year I'll be a tall column of violet flame. Then I'm a guy in a cardigan again. Nobody heals faster than me, I just can't commit to a shape.

1311b3e77aa7.text: My house has chicken legs. People think that's magic. That's a mortgage problem. Last week it walked to Ukraine because it smelled good mushrooms. The appraiser is standing in a bog at 2pm with his little clipboard. "Baba, the house is gone." Of course it's gone. It gets bored. I had to take a bus to a different country and talk to my own front door like a dog that ran away.

9fb351ef4711.text: They kicked me out of the forest last year. Zoning. My hut has chicken legs, you can't just park a giant chicken house in a protected wetland. So now I rent. Ground floor apartment, three floors up. My chicken hut still stands in the woods, empty, twelve Airbnb reviews, all four stars. "Charming but the door moves at night." I miss those legs. I have to walk now like a fool.

899ad5aadd5d.text: I charge people two hundred kroner an hour to help them find their meaning. Meanwhile I spent forty minutes today negotiating with my dishwasher. Do I run it half empty or wait for two more cups. That is the full scope of my purpose now. Full load, half load. Ingrid in Tromsø survived a war on one meal a day. She would see me, and she would end me.

9934bdb4cbc8.text: My therapist told me to find a hygge hobby. Something grounding. So I started baking kanelboller. Now I have a standing appointment with an 8am cardamom situation and no life insight at all. Just a really productive yeast and a growing understanding that cinnamon is basically emotional support spice. My therapist says I'm healing. I say I have 400 grams of flour left.

e3141d84b5cf.text: A monk asked me how I stay so calm. I said I'm not calm, I'm just low-effort. Nothing in this world is worth raising my voice about, except the printer at the office that jams every single time and yet acts so offended when you touch it. Even then, I don't yell. I just stand there, holding the paper, looking at it, the way you look at someone you've already forgiven.

206f7c131455.text: I reached enlightenment in a self-checkout at Target. The screen said unexpected item in bagging area. There was no item. I stared at the empty bagging area for a long time. That's the entire teaching, right there. I'm not going to explain it. If you didn't feel it, you didn't feel it.

943adc2daf3f.text: I bought a greeting card at CVS. It said "Thinking of You." Four dollars and seventy-nine cents for three words I've never once said out loud to a person. You know what I actually think about people? I think they're using the self-checkout wrong. That's the honest card. That's the card that costs four seventy-nine.

4b8210961484.text: My job is mostly paperwork. I'm a chaneque ranger, and ninety percent of my day is filing incident reports because a chaneque hid Doña Remedios' keys under a ceiba root again. That's not wildlife management, that's a lost and found with imps. I carry a clipboard through the jungle so a two-foot goblin can feel alive.

7c8b0f6b6c46.text: I'm a chaneque ranger. People think that's mystical. It's paperwork. I hid a man's keys for three days and my supervisor wrote me up. Formal counseling. For keys. Meanwhile a bear is eating a tourist's sandwich right there, badge numbers 4 through 11 just watching. Nobody documents the bear. You know how many incident reports I filed for one squirrel who looked at me sideways? Four. Typed them myself.

f25a4e2afba1.text: They gave me a badge and a radio like I wasn't born in a ceiba tree. First day of orientation they spent forty minutes on the lost-and-found log. I can curse a man to wander the same trail until his knees give out, but no, I have to initial every water bottle. Karen in accounting has a drawer of thirty-one Hydro Flasks and none of them are haunted.

34d67b78a1cc.text: I bought a label maker. That's my personality now. I labeled the toothpaste. I labeled the butter. My fridge looks like an evidence locker. My roommate asked why everything says BUTTER and I said so nobody's confused, and he looked at me like I'd lost it, which I have, slowly, one label at a time.

f7a1af6385d5.text: I bought a new toothbrush and it came with a cap. A cap. For a toothbrush. Like it's a witness in a federal case. I have to protect its identity now. I'm taking it to brunch under a hat and a fake name. "This is Brad, he does nothing, please don't photograph him."

7ffe8596066d.text: My aura reading came back indigo, which apparently means I'm a spiritual host of light. My friends just call it the couch nobody's allowed to sit on. Last week I spent forty minutes arranging coasters for people who never showed up. That's indigo. It's not enlightenment, it's a group text about potluck sign-ups.

c65366b85490.text: People ask what I do for a living. I live in a barrel. That's it, that's the whole career. They say you should have a backup plan. My backup plan is a second barrel. Alexander comes by, blocks my sun, asks what I want. I say I'd like him to move. He moves. That's a better pension than most men work forty years for.

d6c8a2c42fae.text: I live in a ceramic tub on the street, and the one thing nobody warns you about is the acoustics. Every stomach growl echoes like a amphitheater. Plato walks by, asks what I'm eating, and I say nothing, and my gut answers for me loud enough for the Agora to hear. He called it shameless. I called it lunch.

8297effe35dc.text: I've been in this tub so long the algae pays rent. People say, "Get a hobby." I have a hobby. I lie here and watch Alexander the Great stand over me blocking my sun. He's got the whole world to conquer and he's awkwardly hovering like a clerk at a deli counter. "Can I get you anything?" Yeah, you can move. That's the whole bit.

484e14b72167.text: I did a gig last Tuesday in a pub where the radiator clanged every time someone flushed upstairs. Not once — every time. So now I've got a set rhythm going, I pause for the flush, I wait for the clang, and the crowd thinks that's the bit. I got a standing ovation from a toilet. That's the level I'm operating at. Plumbing timing.

76a419353b6c.text: Being a gig fairy sounds magical. It's not. It's 2 a.m. in a Travelodge, eating a Pot Noodle with a plastic fork, wondering if I should have become an accountant like me mum said. Last week I got booked for a children's party. Sixteen toddlers, one of them bit me. The parents still left a bad review. Said I wasn't "enchanting enough."

4da030781791.text: I'm a fairy, which sounds magical until you see the paperwork. I granted a guy a wish last Tuesday and he asked if I take Venmo. My wings aren't for flying anymore, they're for hovering over DoorDash bags so the burrito stays warm.

05e7b1c17091.text: The rabbits chewed through the petunias again. Fine. That's a violation of Subsection 4B, and I will be issuing a written warning. They don't care. They just sit there, all ears and impunity, like they've got a lawyer on retainer. Meanwhile I've got a gavel made out of a painted acorn and I will use it.

99c390c90cac.text: I send the violation notices myself. Every Tuesday, out before dawn, little gnome waddling up the driveways with a clipboard. Not even a real clipboard — it's a popsicle stick and a leaf. But the Bylaws Section 4, Paragraph C doesn't require letterhead, Karen. It requires intent. And I have been intent since 1997.

a6457bc808aa.text: My doctor's office reads my mind, but only while I'm on hold. I'm thinking about my rash and the voice says your call is important to us. I think about switching to the ob-gyn next door and the hold music skips a beat. One-sided telepathy. They know what I'm about to say before I say it, which is more than my wife manages.

f28a2e26b2e3.text: Your doctor reads your chart and starts thinking at you. I caught the whole diagnosis before he said it out loud. Herniated disc, he's thinking. I'm thinking, yes, that's what WebMD said three weeks ago, Doug. One-sided telepathy is just a guy thinking while you nod. My wife does it in Target. I'm standing there holding a candle that smells like a fireplace and she's already divorcing me in her head.

9f2e172b0943.text: The Preston ruling gave me a migraine that lasted nine days. My wife said it was stress. It was not stress, it was a legal precedent settling behind my eyes. Now every time I get a headache I check the docket. Last week it was just dehydration, but I filed it anyway.

4571c4fa2121.text: Tenant called me at eleven p.m., whispering, like the freezer was armed. Said it was going click-click-click. That's ice, Harold. That's just ice doing what ice does. I hung up and stood at the sink eating a slice of ham, no plate, no light on, and I thought, this is my life now, I own a building.

88e2b1be4e16.text: Tenant texts me a photo of a spider. Not a daddy longlegs, a full tarantula-looking thing sitting on his shower curtain like it pays rent. He wants to know if I'm sending someone. I'm the someone. I'm 68, I've got a slipper and a jar, and this is my building, so now I'm in there in my bathrobe negotiating with an arachnid over a man who won't touch a dish.

71a06c94dc07.text: I tell people I'm a landlord, they get this look, like I'm charging eight hundred for a closet. I am. But the closet has crown molding I installed myself, and my back has never been the same. Last week a tenant texts me at midnight because the smoke detector chirped. I drove over in my slippers, changed the battery, she hands me a casserole. That's the job. Real estate with a side of being somebody's mother.

2df9f2a02563.text: My husband came home from work and said he had "a day." I said tell me about it. He said it would take too long. So I just wrote "a day" in the ledger under Tuesday. Wednesday he says he had "another one." I'm keeping a record. Someday I'm going to audit this marriage and there will be thousands of days, none of them documented, all of them apparently exhausting.

660d13135188.text: The fitted sheet is the only object in your house that refuses to be folded. You watch the video, you do the little triangle thing, and it still comes out looking like a haunted pillowcase. So I ball it up and shove it in the back of the closet, which is where all honesty goes to die.

aa0701103585.text: The medical exam was the worst part, not because of the probe — I've had worse at the VA — but because they took samples and never explained the results. Three years later I'm still waiting on a callback. That's the real horror. You get abducted, examined, and then you're just another guy in the waiting room.

6653e850719e.text: They put me in stirrups for the reproductive extraction and called it a "wellness check." Fine. Then a nurse asked if I wanted the fetus returned standard or premium, like I'm picking a trim level on a leased hybrid. I said standard. She clicked a tongue. Sir, that's the one with the human reflexes.

a90ecebccee4.text: They put the hybrid babies in these glass cribs in the nursery, like a really upscale daycare. And honestly it's just cosmic HR. They gave us a tour and the woman would not stop talking about the benefits package. One of the babies was just floating sideways in its tank and she's like "yeah, Brayden's napping." I have never seen a more normal thing look so deeply wrong.

d60853fb4fd5.text: They told me I was engineered for a better workforce. Turns out the workforce is just me, and I'm doing fine, not great. My performance review was a scan. My manager beeped at me once and then left for a nebula. I've had this job for three years with zero feedback. I don't even know if I'm allowed to be sad about that.

10e3eb256044.text: I owe my guy twelve hundred dollars and I've been paying it back in cucumbers. He said no at first but then he looked at the cucumbers and looked at me and realized I'm not exactly a threat. Now he asks how the garden's doing before he asks about the money. Last week he tried to charge me interest. In basil.

0b1240c0c9e3.text: I owe my buddy fourteen cucumbers. Fourteen. From a bet in July. He brings it up every time, like I forgot. Bro, I'm not avoiding you, I just keep buying the wrong vegetables. Last week I showed up with a zucchini and he looked at me like I handed him Monopoly money.

aba8098da3de.text: I told my buddy he owed me a cucumber from 2019 and he acted like I was being dramatic. Bro, you watched me eat that entire salad out of respect for you. You looked me in the eye. Now it's 2025 and I'm showing up with a spreadsheet. You think I want to be the cucumber guy? You made me the cucumber guy.

ff8c85f0c850.text: My kid's sumo coach is a kappa. A river spirit. He weighs forty pounds and he steals my son's vegetables at practice. Last week he looked me dead in the eye, held up a cucumber, and said "this is his lunch now." I pay this guy $120 a month. He doesn't have a bank account. He lives in a drainage ditch behind the rec center.

3244549a0c47.text: The greys pull me through my car window every Tuesday. I stopped locking the doors, it's just easier. My neighbor watched me float through the windshield and asked if I'd gotten my eyes checked. I said the vision's fine, it's the parking that's the problem.

1d352776bcaf.text: The alien paralyzed me mid-scream once, and the worst part was my mouth stayed open the whole time. Just jaw hanging, no sound. I'd been screaming about something stupid too. When they finally let me move, my neck was sore from the draft. Even the paralysis is amateur hour. Nothing about my abduction has ever gone smoothly.

7f87e84484ba.text: The aliens didn't even abduct me, they scheduled me. Noon, calendar invite, "quarterly hybrid program sync." I'm lying on the table paralyzed, can't move, can't scream, and one of them is asking if I've updated my skills profile. I floated through my own car window to get here and they still want two factors of authentication.

d4be9e0e8d44.text: I don't even do the abducting anymore. That's Kevin's job. Kevin's a Gray, thin little guy, works hard, never complains, but he can't read a room. Last Tuesday he brought me the wrong specimen. I said Kevin, this is a man from Toledo, I asked for a woman from Toledo. He just blinked. They blink a lot. I've been doing this for eleven thousand years and I still have to fix paperwork.

d2feaf7dc39a.text: I dispatch two Grays for every job. Not because we're short-staffed, it's just review season and nobody wants to do their quarterly abductions. I sign the forms, I dot the fields, and then I stare at you with four thousand lenses for two seconds, which in HR terms counts as a written warning.

b6395e253473.text: The abduction itself is easy. The hard part is the paperwork. I approve expense reports for four Grays who keep putting "human subject transportation" as the line item when it's clearly just a van. Last quarter one of them expensed a coffee. A coffee. We don't even drink coffee. I flagged it, he flagged me back, and now we're both in mediation.

7b449d5b4ad1.text: The worst part of the job is the vest. It's not cut for wings, so the straps ride up into my armpits and the reflective strip only covers one shoulder. I keep having to turn sideways so cars can see me, and then the kids think I'm doing a little dance. I got a 401k now.

0badb5c5025e.text: He left and came back three days later just to return my hoe. Three days! I didn't even notice it was gone. Turns out he'd been running errands in the ship — you can hear him, a sewing-machine sound across the whole valley, him flossing and hydrating somewhere over Iowa. He hands me the hoe, says "hydrate, brother," and ascends back up there.

eaa3a0a4d49c.text: My ship can fold space in half and I still can't load a dishwasher. Back home there are no junk drawers, one utensil per drawer, clean counters. When I described junk drawers to the Council of Zeta Reticuli, they went quiet the exact way your grandma goes quiet when you tell her you do podcasts.

b70792d2e9ed.text: Look, I don't want a cult. I got a ship, I got a message, I got a sewing machine in the cargo bay that hums in B-flat. But mostly I got chores. You know how long it takes to beam a man's hoe back to the exact spot he left it in the garden. Twelve minutes. I could conquer Jupiter in that time. Instead I'm standing in your yard with a metal detector for lost gardening tools.

e76d718ec99a.text: I hosted my sister's hatchling's coming-of-scales ceremony last month. Two hundred reptiles in my living room. My nephew shed on the rug and everyone just... walked around it. My niece tells me, "Aunt Vess, that's what the shed is for, you absorb through it." I said no, Brenda, that's what a vacuum is for. She looked at me like I suggested eating the hatchlings. Anyway, the rug is ruined. Eighty years of bloodline heritage, gone.

a669221590e4.text: My doctor told me I need to cut back on salt. Salt! I used to run a bloodline. I controlled a continent through fear and cold-blooded politics. And now a man named Gary with a soft handshake is telling me about my sodium. I could eat Gary. Nobody would even miss him. But I can't. Because of the salt thing.

01006c19257a.text: People see me and jump. Sir, I'm just trying to buy a rotisserie chicken at King Soopers. You think I want to be here? I'm cold-blooded, this parking lot is forty degrees, and I'm only in line because my kids like the one with the barbecue sauce packet. Last week a lady fainted in aisle seven and my first thought was, good, free chicken.

ab8db1bcaf16.text: People ask if I'm cold-blooded like it's a personality flaw. Sir, I pay taxes in Loveland, Colorado. I'm at the DMV for three hours on a Tuesday. You think I'm not cold-blooded? I'm the most emotionally dead one in that building and I'm not even the reptile.

a2d2bb220556.text: I deliver packages in Loveland and people always do the double-take at my scales, like that's the weird part. Ma'am, I have your refrigerated insulin in a plastic bag I'm holding with my teeth. I'm a gecko in cargo shorts doing the Lord's work. You want a signature or you want your meds?

9714a747068a.text: My manager scheduled a meeting to discuss why we have too many meetings. Forty-five minutes. Solved it. Then she scheduled a follow-up. I said, 'Deborah, that's the follow-up.' She said, 'No, this is the prep for the follow-up.' I sat there perfectly still, which comes easy to me. I've been in that building so long I forgot what outside smells like. Just recycled air and somebody's yogurt.

9ebd63e61a05.text: My boss asked me to circle back on the Q3 numbers, so I circled back, and he wasn't there. That's the whole job. I approved a four dollar expense report yesterday and then had to get that four dollar expense report approved. The approval cost more than the expense. I ate a mouse under my desk just to feel something and had to submit that too, mileage.

8e321e1d5dda.text: I'm an intern at Bloodline. Reptilian bloodline, obviously. My whole job is shredding documents — that's the gig, I'm a lizard who went to college. My mom keeps asking when I'm gonna use my degree. Mom, I eat mice off the floor for free. They promised me a global takeover. I run the copier.

eb516fec86fd.text: My supervisor told me to update the spreadsheet, so I did, but with my tongue, because that's how I click. Nobody said anything. Devon from accounting just stared at his monitor for a full minute and then went to lunch. I'm three weeks into this internship and I've learned that humans will accept literally anything if it happens near a Tuesday.

2bbb2ce2d19e.text: I shed, and my roommate wants the skins for a jacket. Buddy, that's my skin. You don't buy a raincoat off a guy's back. Fine, I sold him one. He wore it to the office, got asked if it was real, said "yeah, it's my roommate's." I lost a layer and my dignity in one afternoon.

d3262a47cc9d.text: My cousin started selling thessian shed-skins as "artisanal leather" at the farmers market. He's got a whole booth now. He calls it "ethically sourced, single-molt." I went by to support him. A lady asked if it was vegan. He said, "Ma'am, this thing ate a chicken to make this jacket." She bought two. That's the customer base. People who want to feel ethical but also want to eat the chicken.

1ba7ef5c39e6.text: You ever try on a thessik garment in the store? Just a normal fitting room, normal fluorescent lighting, and I'm standing there in this reptilian thing, watching the scales catch light like a wet pool noodle. The lady comes to the door and goes, "How's the fit?" And I genuinely don't know. It fits like skin fits, which is the whole problem with skin, isn't it. I said, "It's tight in the tail." She wrote that down.

e070a33ad8d7.text: I'm a reptile in Calgary, so winter is just a slow dimmer switch on my entire personality. People ask if I hibernate. No, man, I file T4s like everyone else, I just do it cold. My coworker Brenda asked me to autograph her kid's dinosaur drawing. I signed it. That's my cousin Gary. We don't talk.

dc38b564bf56.text: I've been wearing this human suit nine months straight. My elbow itches and I can't scratch it, I have to go to the bathroom and unlatch my forearm. My dry contacts are worse. I put in drops at 7 a.m., by noon my left eye is rolling back like a demon in an old movie while my right one keeps perfect time.

dfe8fb00f9a3.text: Ralph denied my transfer out of Dulce again. Sixteenth denial. Said my bloodline review wasn't conclusive, whatever that means, I've been down here eleven thousand years. I just want a window. Not even sunlight, I'll take a fake one from IKEA. He said no. The thermostat's still at sixty-two and I've got a thin hide, or thick, depends on the day.

1442bb755833.text: I asked a lady where her air filter was and she pointed at the vent like that's where the dirt goes to die. Ma'am, that's a grate. That's just a grate. That's like pointing at your mouth and saying that's where your stomach is. I had to get on the roof to fix her problem she diagnosed with a wall.

8b9939b10560.text: Thermostat's got a schedule feature now. It knows I leave at 7:40 and drop to 62 degrees like I'm punishing the house. Then at 6:55pm it kicks back up to 70, welcoming me home. I don't get that from my wife. The furnace is out there in the dark going, he's coming, he's coming, everyone look busy.

f698a20a3e48.text: Guy called me his third favorite person behind his wife and a guy who cut him off in traffic. I fixed his AC. He handed me a glass of ice water like it was communion. I stood in 118 degrees in his attic so he could watch Netflix without sweating, and I'm supposed to be grateful for the tap water.

df322e6b88d4.text: Everyone assumes I'm out here tracking elk or communing with the watershed. No, ma'am, I'm a government employee. My job is to walk eight miles a day so I can tell a guy in Hokas that his dog poop bag is not biodegradable just because it's green. Last week I cited a man for leaving a bag on the trail and he said, "It's compostable, it says so on the box." Sir, I have a clipboard and a state vehicle. Please step away from the juniper.

9c9585074245.text: They gave me the clipboard. I'm nine feet tall, I've been reported as a "possible bear" forty times this month, and now I'm checking off "non-native thistle" on a laminated form. My handwriting is a paw print. Somebody flagged it.

d5d8b447dd9c.text: My job is picking up trash on a trail and nobody ever asks about that, they only ask where I've been sighted. Sir, I was at the recycling center. I filled out a form. Bigfoot has a form. I bent down to grab a Gatorade bottle and three hikers filmed me and I just stood there holding it, because that's the job. They blurred my face anyway.

7f1fbf0eca4a.text: Wish in writing must specify whether "unlimited wishes" means infinite or just, you know, a lot. Ambiguity kills cases. Woman came in last week, wants "infinite pizza." Okay. Toppings? She says, all of them. All at once. Every topping. I said that's not pizza, that's a crime scene. She says, infinite crime scene pizza then. I billed her for six hours.

ce666d167b6d.text: People think granting wishes is glamorous. It's not. It's paperwork. I spent three hours last Tuesday arguing with a guy over whether "I wish I had more time" covers a fourth snooze button. It doesn't. That's not a wish, that's a sleep disorder. And I have to bill him. By the hour. For saying no.

a22bfa71938b.text: I had a guy come in yesterday and he wants to wish his wife loved him again. I told him, sir, that is not a wish, that is a therapy referral, and I pushed him down the hall to Dr. Miftah's office. He still wanted to fill out the form. People love the form more than the wish.

4d438817107c.text: Everyone who gets abducted describes the same boring stuff — bright light, cold table, weird instruments. Nobody ever says they got a sandwich. You'd think an advanced civilization could whip up a turkey club. "Sorry you're scared, here's some chips." At least then I'd have a story worth telling at work.

037d10485af0.text: Grandma saw a fairy behind the barn in 1931, same as a woman in Ohio saw a grey alien behind a barn in 2004. Same barn energy, different press kit. The fairy had wings, the alien has a spaceship. Both of them took something. Grandma lost an hour, the woman lost two. You know what happened in that hour? Probably nothing. That's the horror.

8a0d9a58d1e0.text: We send a human intermediary, guy in a full space helmet, mid-abduction. Standard protocol. He's supposed to calm you down. He asks for your insurance card. You just caught an energy blast, you're hiding under a metal table, and this man wants to know if you're in-network. Then he floats out. Five witnesses, five days, nobody believes a word of it. Meanwhile I'm the one still holding his clipboard.

6fce4bce5ddf.text: They call it an energy blast like it's a superpower. It's not. It's a guy — I'm assuming it's a guy, I couldn't tell, there's no HR on that ship — and he points a thing at me and it hits me in the shoulder. Not the chest, not the head. The shoulder. Like a bad masseuse. And the worst part? I jumped first. I jumped, and THEN it got me. So now I'm not even a victim, I'm just bad at jumping. Five days I've been telling people this and everybody's first question is always, "Why'd you jump?

6cc8ad1e3c4a.text: I narrate snow the way those Attenborough guys narrate lions. The drift is moving east, it has claimed the mailbox. My neighbors don't hear weather, they hear me on the porch at 6am going, light flurries, cumulative and unbothered. Last week the plow guy asked if I'd do his wedding. I said only if it snows indoors.

2556dd83e942.text: The weather app says two inches by morning, so I'm at the window at 11pm like I'm watching a stakeout. It's just snow, man. It lands on the Wendy's dumpster exactly the way it lands on the Matterhorn. My job is to describe it anyway, so: flakes. They're falling. Very slowly. Over the parking lot.

e568dbe02a8e.text: I narrate snow. That's the whole job. People assume it's dramatic — it's not. Last week I watched a man scrape his windshield for eleven minutes and all I could say was the ice wins. My mother wanted me to be a doctor. My mother also wanted the driveway shoveled by somebody, and look how that worked out for her.

95be0aea92f9.text: I went to the coffee shop and the girl asked my name for the cup. I said Zeus. She wrote Sue. I thought about smiting her, but honestly, Sue's a fine name. My thunderbolt's in the car anyway. The coffee was four dollars and it was cold by the time I got to the parking lot.

cd45c74d432b.text: Loading the dishwasher is the closest I get to a Tetris championship. I'm in there rearranging spatulas like I'm defusing a bomb. My wife loads it like a yard sale, closes her eyes, shoves the door shut, prays. Then it does that thing where it leaks onto the floor and we both act surprised. It's a ritual at this point. We mop, we lie, we move on.

8e9fe8ed7f52.text: I tried ordering a pizza last week. They asked for my address. I said Mount Olympus. The guy put me on hold twice. Then he came back and goes, "We don't deliver to the clouds, sir." My father is literally the god of the sky and this teenager is lecturing me about delivery zones. I thundered at him. He charged me a delivery fee anyway.

6d0726166714.text: They got that self-checkout talking. "Unexpected item in the bagging area." I put the bag there. You told me to put the bag there, now it's unexpected? And I'm standing in there like I just got caught. "Sorry, sorry, my bad." I'm paying for this! Buying milk and apologizing to a machine that can't find its own charger.

4c57a573cb00.text: I love self-checkout until it turns on me. 'Unexpected item in bagging area.' I put it there. You watched me put it there. We both saw it happen. Now I'm standing there waiting for a teenager to come approve my life choices. The machine don't trust me. The machine never trusted me. I been scanning my own groceries for ten years and it still acts like I'm stealing.

06f14cb491df.text: Everybody says they love their neighborhood. Then you ask them what street they live on and they say "Oh, I actually moved to Scottsdale." You don't love your neighborhood. You love that a bodega would sell you a loosie at 3am. That's not love, that's a drug habit with a zip code.

0a2423f73c35.text: My landlord raised my rent during the pandemic. Not because he needed the money. He lives in Scottsdale. He just read an article. That's the game now. Somebody in another state reads a number, and a whole neighborhood has to eat less. And then they call us essential.

87f20396197e.text: You go to the dentist, he's got both hands in your mouth, and he says, so how often do you floss? Sir. You know I don't floss. This is a shakedown.

af874e3d3034.text: They don't fire you anymore, they let you go. As if you were a balloon. Then there's restructuring, which is firing you wearing a necktie. And my favorite is pursuing other opportunities, like the opportunity to eat.

b0a396f11140.text: They say "passed away" now, like the guy just stepped out for a minute. My uncle passed away, we're all standing around the casket, my aunt says he's in a better place. He's in Newark. The better place is Newark. Meanwhile the funeral home calls it a "celebration of life." There's a guy in a box. Somebody's eating a cookie. That's not a celebration, that's a crime scene with refreshments.

07186ac5cd67.text: they call it a restroom. there's no rest in it. nobody's resting in there, they're negotiating with their own body at a gas station off I-95. that's not a euphemism, that's a crime scene report.

503bc7f5de7c.text: The airline seatbelt sign is the only rule in America you can break if you're sneaky enough. You can't run a red light by walking confidently. But the seatbelt dings off, everyone stands up, and we all pretend we didn't just try to open a door at thirty thousand feet. We're not a civilization. We're a group of adults playing musical chairs with a parachute.

6c724b1d2418.text: "How are you" is the biggest lie we tell, and we do it forty times a day. Nobody has ever answered it. Somebody says "how are you" and you say "good, you?" and they say "good." Two people just exchanged a full health report in under a second, both lying, both fine with it. It's the only survey where the results are determined before the question is asked.

243c3b43a04a.text: "How are you." Nobody wants an answer to that. Nobody in the history of the greeting has wanted an answer. You say "how are you," I say "good," we both move on — that's the deal. But once a year some maniac says "actually, my back's been killing me," and the whole room freezes. You asked for the weather, he handed you an MRI.

1888243c4353.text: My daughter asked me why I stare at my phone so much. I said I'm looking at pictures of you. She said, "I'm right here." Yeah, and you're asleep at 7:30, sweetheart. This is the only version of you that doesn't need something.

e36e38fb93e4.text: My daughter asked me what I do at work all day and I had to explain comedy to a child. I said I make people laugh and she said why. I said that's a good question, I've been asking myself the same thing for twenty years. She said I think you should get a real job. Six years old, already building a case.

f546e2869170.text: My kid asked me why we stop at a red light

fb3abce3fed4.text: The vending machine at work knows I'm coming. It hears my footsteps down the hall and thinks, oh, him again, with his quarters. I once watched it dispense a bag of chips to nobody. Just gave them away. I think it was trying to make a friend before I got there.

aee28148f0d1.text: I pressed B7 for chips and the machine dropped pretzels. Now I gotta sit with that. A vending machine is just a god with a coin slot, handing you what you get, not what you want. I've had roommates with less insight. They just ate my yogurt.

1102dd1daa73.text: The vending machine is a metaphysics professor. It tells you exactly what you'll get, and you still feel betrayed when it happens. I bought pretzels once and got a bag of air with a few salt crystals living in it. That's not a snack, that's a haunted house in snack clothing.

3243301eb23a.text: The self-checkout machine at Walmart accuses you of theft, but politely. Unexpected item in bagging area.

8d4f686f47a0.text: I bought a bread maker. My wife said that's the most exciting thing that's happened in this house since the dryer broke. I said you have no respect for the bread maker. She said you've used it twice. I said yeah, and both times I had to open the bag myself anyway. It's a hat for bread.

a14efbdec9e3.text: There's a man ahead of me at the pharmacy paying in exact change and people behind us are sighing. I tell them, relax. He's not holding you up, he's holding you together. That man is buying blood pressure medication. It's an old joke that you never see a U-Haul behind a hearse, and it's the only one I know that's actually true.

f490bbf64b6d.text: People think living in the inner Earth is magical. It's an HOA with 100 cities and one government. My neighbor's crystal array grew two inches over the property line, and Shambhala filed a complaint. Same as up here, just with better Wi-Fi and no sun.

0020f337e216.text: Went to a client's house and their smoke detector was chirping. Just one chirp every forty seconds. Nobody acknowledged it. I'm sitting there filling out paperwork, waiting for it, like it's my job to fix it. Four chirps in, I stopped writing. I just... listened. We're all just pretending that isn't happening. That chirp is the house's heartbeat and nobody's checked on it in six years.

9f9e93e0efc4.text: The inspector showed up unannounced, which I guess is the whole point of an inspection. He spent eleven minutes measuring a doorframe with a little metal ruler like he was solving a murder. Then he looked at me and said, "So, who lives here?" My guy, you have my driver's license in your hand. You tell me.

4661e28f62d2.text: I had a field visit scheduled for Tuesday between ten and two, which is four hours, which is not a window, that's a marriage. The guy shows up at 1:58, clipboard in hand, looks at my meter and goes, "Yep, that's a meter." Took him ninety seconds. I rearranged my whole life to watch a man confirm the existence of an object I look at every day.

0ac3878e8e8a.text: My grandmother told me I inherited Anansi's cunning, the trickster spider's gift for outsmarting everyone. Then I spent forty minutes yesterday untangling my earbuds and talking to them, saying things like "okay, we're almost there." Turns out the cunning is just patience and a little saliva.

5bd1f9902289.text: People love that Anansi owns all the stories. Meanwhile I own a web, and a mortgage on the web. A fly got stuck Tuesday, I wrapped him up, went to sleep, woke up Wednesday and he'd already paid rent. I'm not a trickster. I'm a landlord with eight legs and no Wi-Fi.

f1e984691dc5.text: I slide into your DMs while you're asleep. People call it dream communication, I call it a 3am work email you can't ignore. You wake up thinking you had a deep dream about your grandmother, and I'm like, that was a note about your posture. Cosmic Reiki doesn't book itself, Karen.

5d07f1d3866e.text: People say they can feel my healing beam, but most of you just use me as a night light. I'm hovering over your bed at 3am trying to realign your chakras and you roll over muttering "close the door." I'm light-based. I don't have a door. That's the whole issue.

6cb675082b69.text: My hut walks on chicken legs, so nothing in that house is ever level. I've been living on a tilt for six hundred years and my lower back is a war crime. The children wander in expecting a metaphor and I have to tell them I'm just a woman with sciatica and a mortar and pestle full of aspirin.

ceea01ac1bad.text: My house walks. On chicken legs. People think that's the hard part. No, the hard part is the mail. The postman has been leaving my letters in the same birch grove for thirty years. I moved six hundred feet. He did not. Now I walk out every morning in my nightgown, down the hill, in the mud, to find out if I'm still approved for a credit card.

bbba020cfd32.text: The weather app is the only thing I check daily and act shocked by every single time. Oh, rain again? In Norway? In November? Who could have known. I say "who could have known" out loud, alone, while holding an umbrella and looking directly at the rain. I'm not a person, I'm a background character in a video game repeating the same line when you walk past.

60fe821f9894.text: I tried to meal prep on Sunday. That's the Nordic dream, you know. Twelve identical containers of kylling and quinoa lined up like little soldiers. By Tuesday I'm staring at container number four thinking, no. No, I deserve a croissant. I am a woman of depth and complexity. I need a pastry with layers. So I ate the croissant over the container and put the container back in the fridge. Meal prepped for the trash.

d403c2f49d2a.text: I'm a Nordic life coach, so my whole pitch is moderation. Lagom — not too much, not too few. My client wanted a five-year plan, I told her to start with the junk drawer. She got to the rubber bands and whispered, "Is this it?" Yes, Astrid. That is literally the point.

677cb2d2fa07.text: They ask what I attained under the Bodhi tree. Peace. Complete, unshakable peace. Then I sat on the 405 and a man in a lifted truck ate a burrito in my blind spot, and I thought, oh, this is the work. Enlightenment didn't end the errands. It just made me present for them.

aa7697579c83.text: Enlightenment doesn't fix anything practical. I sat in perfect inner peace at the laundromat for forty minutes watching my jeans go around, thinking that pair's done, no wait, those are mine. Nirvana is having no wants, which is easy when the dryer still has eleven minutes left on the display that means nothing.

d1f434919270.text: I tried to meditate this morning. Got distracted by a crack in the ceiling. I stared at that crack for forty minutes, which I'm told is technically meditation, but my teacher calls it "avoiding work." Either way, I found inner peace. The crack is still there, but now I accept it.

51fc42824c80.text: My abuela swore the chaneque would drown me if I crossed the creek. Then I met him. He's not a demon, he's a ranger with a clipboard. He asked for my permit to be terrified. I said I don't have one. He said, "Then you're not scared, you're trespassing." Now I pay twelve dollars a year to be haunted.

3af84939cba7.text: I'm a chaneque ranger, so my job is guarding ancient ruins, but the tourists just ask where the bathroom is. There is no bathroom. There's a thousand-year-old pyramid and a guy in a fanny pack asking me to unlock it. I tell him it's closed for restoration. He asks me if it's wheelchair accessible. Sir, it was built by people who didn't have wheels.

0e15e366d6e8.text: They made me a chaneque ranger, which sounds mystical. It's not. It's ninety percent forms because a goblin moved a tourist's car keys four feet. Yesterday one hid a woman's sandal in a pine and I had to write 'shoe, tree, west side' on a report nobody reads. The chaneques think this job is hilarious. My supervisor thinks I'm drunk.

7940ceb15528.text: The self-checkout machine at Kroger accuses me of theft every trip. Unexpected item in the bagging area. It's my wallet, I'm paying you. I'm standing there patting my pockets like a cop pulled me over while a twelve-year-old bags seventeen cucumbers and stares. Last week I just left the cart and walked out. I don't even need the groceries anymore. I need closure.

d1e322d36a83.text: Grocery stores put the milk in the back so you walk past everything else. That's not retail, that's a hostage situation with coupons. I went in for two percent and came out with a garden hose I don't own a yard for. The hose wasn't even on sale. I just looked at it and it looked back.

482d81f77881.text: Every morning I do a spiritual practice. It's called putting away the dishes. I match the Tupperware lids to the containers and that's the closest I get to enlightenment. You put a big lid on a small container, that's karma. That lid comes back. My mother told me that. She was not a monk, she was from Queens, but she was right.

a17b1966e7e7.text: I sleep in a large clay pot. People hear that and get sad for me. Don't be. You know what a tub is? It's a bed with walls. I don't fall out. The wind hits the outside and I don't even feel it. You people with your mattresses, your pillows, your thread count — you're just lying in the middle of a field pretending you're safe. I'm in a hole on purpose. I'm the only honest man in this city.

ab052d73450a.text: I lived in a clay jar. Not a house, a jar. People said that's poverty. That's not poverty. Poverty is having twelve cups and using none of them. I saw a boy crouch at a stream, cup his hands, drink. I threw my cup in the bushes. It was a nice cup. That's the part that costs you. Everybody talks about the giving things up. Nobody talks about the good cup.

92e082ca57f0.text: Plato says he's seeking the Form of the Good. I've seen the man eat breakfast. He gets a fig, wipes it on his toga, and calls it a meal. That's the Form of the Good right there — a fig, slightly dirty. But that's not philosophy to him, that's just a Tuesday.

4b8d55d7a520.text: The fairy godmother showed up to my apartment unannounced, started rearranging my kitchen. I said, "You're not fixing my life, that's a hoarding problem." She waved a wand at my sink full of dishes and made them sparkle. Sparkle. Still dirty. Now every mug is glittering at me like it knows I'll get to it tomorrow. That's the fairy magic I needed. A wand that turns my avoidance into ambiance.

7828be85325b.text: People think being a gig fairy is magical. It's not. Last week I worked a kids' birthday party in Slough and the mum asked if I could "make it more fairy" while I was stuck in a cupboard with a broken wand and a parking ticket. That's the job. Sparkles and municipal despair.

2d45b5f02ae0.text: Being a gig fairy sounds magical until you realize my whole job is finding open mic slots for comics who then complain the flyer font is wrong. I have wings. Actual wings. And my biggest accomplishment last week was convincing a bar owner to turn on the second light so people could see the stage. He called it a health and safety concession. I call it a miracle. Nobody applauds for me. I'm the only fairy alive who gets tipped in beer and unsolicited notes about sound levels.

6ab887cf64d0.text: I got a warning letter for bein two inches off the mulch line. Two inches. Meanwhile Karen's flamingo's been deadbolted to my lawn since March. I didn't say a word. That's the gnome code — we just stand there and judge quietly. It's not a personality, it's a warranty position.

f87ef4debb08.text: I got a warning letter for my own mailbox. Apparently it's 2 inches too tall. I'm a gnome. My whole body is two inches. They're citing me for existing at the correct scale. I'd shrink but then I'd be under the minimum height requirement for gnomes. There's always a committee.

751eed20b0d7.text: People ask if I get bored sitting in the same yard all day. No. My neighbor Carol has a driveway crack she's been staring at for eleven months and she's named it Gerald. I just sit there, watching her have a whole relationship with concrete. That's my television.

f044b11366d9.text: I called the bank about a twelve-dollar fee and I swear I could hear the rep thinking, but it's one-sided, so all I get is his half. It was just hold music with his opinions layered over it. This guy's balance is a rounding error. The fee was legitimate. That's what killed me.

43ece553d862.text: The hold music knows what I did. It's one-sided telepathy, they're broadcasting, I'm just sitting here holding my Social Security number like a bingo card. They play that flute loop until you confess. I called about a forty dollar charge and by the third chorus I'd admitted things my wife still doesn't know. The rep picked up and I just said sorry before she could even ask.

a72eda00711e.text: Everybody thinks one-sided telepathy would be spooky. It's not, it's customer service. I hear my neighbor's whole inner monologue and it's just hold music and grocery lists. Yesterday he was thinking "did I get enough Rotel" for forty-five minutes. That's it. That's the mind-reading. You don't learn anyone's secrets, you just learn they're low on Rotel.

ee091cae68c6.text: 4A called at 2am about a persistent buzzing. It was his own vape alarm going off because he charges it on the radiator like a goddamn iguana. I stood there in my slippers, holding a spatula, and he asks if I can move his recycling bin two feet left. Two feet. That's the job now. I have a master key and a degree in spatial logistics.

af19f99b4dc5.text: Tenants call me about a lightbulb out. A bulb. I go over, I unscrew it, I put a new one in, and they thank me like I rebuilt their kitchen. Meanwhile the guy at 4B has been "paying me in cash and good intentions" since March. I'm not a landlady. I'm a woman with a ladder and a personality disorder.

86dd9c40f27a.text: Every morning I do the same negotiation with my coffee maker. It's a slow drip, so I stand there watching it like it's going to speed up if I glare hard enough. Never does. The coffee's done when it's done, and I'm just a woman in a robe threatening an appliance that runs on electricity and spite.

0090076b99b3.text: The self-checkout at Target judges me. It freezes, scans my face, and says "unexpected item in the bagging area." I'm holding a single candle. I'm not smuggling anything. Last week it locked me out and called a teenager over who looked at me like I'd detonated something. I just wanted the vanilla one that smells like my grandmother's hallway.

657809045227.text: My bank app sends me a notification every time I spend four dollars. Four dollars. Like I'm going to forget. I bought a coffee and got a push alert, a text, and an email. Three notifications for a latte. Meanwhile my actual debt just sits there quietly, like a cat waiting to knock something off the counter.

6ed2c7599374.text: They gave me a full physical, which is more than my doctor in Nashua has ever done. They checked my eyes, my ears, drew some blood. The only thing missing was a clipboard and a pamphlet about high cholesterol. Even the aliens are rationing healthcare.

9b782f554fc1.text: The greys gave me a physical, and it was exactly like my HMO physical, same urgency, same eye contact, same guy going "small pinch" with a instrument the size of a drumstick. I asked what it was for. He said "standard screening." I've had this plan since 1958. Nobody is coming to see you.

3878b0b44fdf.text: The aliens gave me a full physical. And I mean full. Nobody warned me the probe was cold. You'd think beings who crossed the galaxy would spring for a little lubricant. My dentist uses gel for a cleaning, these guys just winged it. And then they act confused when I scream. Dude, I flinch at paper cuts.

33744cf41338.text: They pitched it like a startup. "We're building a better workforce." Sir, you built a species. You're not building a workforce. There's no pizza Fridays in the nursery. It's rows of glass cribs and a guy named Greg with a clipboard. And every hybrid baby gets a five-star rating from the xenobiologist. "This one's a solid B-plus, good work ethic." It's a breeding program with performance reviews. My cousin called. He wants to know if it's a good company. I said they have dental, they rip it out of you and install it in the babies.

b4dc19ca00bf.text: The aliens keep calling it an incubation chamber. It's a nursery. They've got little glass cribs, mobiles made of stars or whatever, and a strict no-crying policy enforced by a low hum that vibrates your teeth. I asked about nap schedules and they said, "We don't believe in sleep." Great. Neither did my last job. At least this one comes with dental.

3e7161364ba5.text: They pitch it like a staffing agency. Sixty thousand embryos in glass cribs, and the alien HR lady's got a clipboard. "We're building a better workforce." Lady, you're building a nursery. There's a cry room. You gave the cry room a fax number.

5c7c5197a3b2.text: I collect cucumber debt. People hear that and act like I said I

d275ab0186d3.text: I owe my buddy twenty bucks for cucumbers. Not a euphemism, just cucumbers. I bought forty dollars worth of cucumbers at the farmers market and my card declined, so he fronted me. Now I'm "in the cucumber game" according to him. He texts me every Friday. Just the cucumber emoji. I don't even eat cucumbers, I was making tzatziki for a girl who ghosted me.

fead6aa93835.text: I ran into my buddy Dave at the grocery store. He owes me eleven cucumbers since July. He saw me, picked up a zucchini, and tried to slide it toward me like that settles anything. That's not a cucumber, Dave. I'm not collecting on a technicality here, but I know what a zucchini is.

13c0569a6edc.text: Self-checkout. I love self-checkout because it's the only job I'll ever have where I can be terrible and no one fires me. I scanned the same bag of rice four times. The machine just said unexpected item. That's not unexpected. I told you. I scanned it three times already.

339fd78e182e.text: Standing in line at the grocery store is just sumo for people who gave up. Nobody's watching, nobody's clapping, but you're still squared up against a woman with 14 items in the express lane holding a coupon from 2019. I lost. She turned around, looked me dead in the eyes, and said, take your time, dear. That's a Yokozuna. She didn't even stretch.

923a76f8e94e.text: My whole recruiting class is one turtle. That's the entire river. I bow to greet him out of respect, my dish water spills, I'm weak, he beats me. Same practice every Tuesday. They make us bow. In a water sport. Six years I've kept this dish level and etiquette ends me.

31fe2f704dbc.text: The hybrid program is just cosmic HR. They show up at 3 a.m., put you through a skills assessment you can't move during, and the whole time you're thinking I have a performance review at work on Thursday. Then they adjust your vibrations and leave without a callback. I didn't get the job. I didn't even get the rejection email.

f8f7d337e362.text: I saw a Harvard psychiatrist about the abductions and he believed every word. Not one skeptical question. I've had friends call me a liar over a two-dollar lunch tab, but this man with two degrees on his wall nodded along like I was describing a parking ticket. That's the controversial part apparently. My friends are more rigorous peer review than Harvard.

ddbd328945db.text: Abduction is mostly administrative. They paralyze you so you can't scream, float you through the car window, change your vibrations, and then just leave. No debrief. My Harvard psychiatrist asked what I felt and I said used. Like a temp who worked the whole quarter and never got the offer letter.

cf46e827f841.text: I do middle management for the abduction. The Grays do the work, I sign the forms. Last week one of them put the speculum in backwards and I had to send a polite email. Nobody above me to complain to. I report to a void, and the void does not do performance reviews. I just stare with four thousand lenses and pretend I'm reading.

09bca51cefc7.text: I run the abductions. Nobody runs me. I direct six Grays, I file reports nobody reads, and last week one of them put a spec sheet upside down on the slab. I didn't yell. I just looked at him with all four thousand lenses until he fixed it. That's management. You don't raise your voice when you have compound eyes, you just let him feel the full perimeter of your disappointment.

90a83b159e4f.text: I got the crossing guard job because they said I had "experience with traffic." One bridge. One time. And now I'm out there every morning at 7:45 with the little yellow sign, and some mom in a Suburban rolls right through the crosswalk like I'm not even standing there with my giant red eyes and my wings folded into a safety vest. Ma'am, I have seen the future. It involves your kid getting clipped by a Honda Civic on Route 2.

7dd763df4c60.text: They gave me the reflective vest. The vest. I have two glowing red eyes and they thought, you know what'd help, high-vis yellow. Now I'm just a guy in a vest at 7:45 in the morning holding a plastic paddle that says STOP, and Brenda from the PTA still won't make eye contact. Lady, I predicted a bridge collapse. You can wave.

2a163113ec77.text: He hands the hoe back before I even ask. Says, you dropped this. Nobody saw me drop it. He just knows where everyone's tools are and he gives them back so nicely you stop checking your pockets. That's not farming help, that's a warning wrapped in a thank you.

5b36e2825d83.text: He handed the hoe back with both hands like a waiters' tray, thanked me for lending it, and I've been living alone for six years so that's the most anyone's spoken to me. Now I floss because a man from Arcturus told me to, and I don't even know if Arcturus is real or just where he parks.

320155030dc0.text: He handed back the hoe and I said thanks, and he said you're welcome, and then we just stood there. Two guys, midday, neither of us leaving first. I put it in the shed. He watched me latch the door like he was checking I knew how.

09d2dc31f7c4.text: My nephew keeps the thermostat at seventy-two and calls it comfortable. I'm a reptile, Karen. That's not comfort, that's a slow cooker with a fan. I retired from matriarchy, not from thermoregulation. Now I sit on his radiator like a cat and he posts it to Facebook with a little heart emoji.

78fcbe621291.text: My niece asked me to babysit her kids. I said honey, I raised seven children to adulthood and only ate two of them, so I think I'm qualified. She said that's exactly why she's nervous. I don't understand the younger generation. I kept my grandchildren alive for a whole weekend. They were slightly crispy by Sunday but that's called roasting, and you people pay good money for it at Applebee's.

2f97ad62f281.text: I'm a reptilian humanoid living in Loveland, Colorado, and the most stressful part of my day is the Homeowners Association. Barb sent out a mass email about my lawn. Lady, I shed. There's skin on the walkway every spring. That's not that. Read your bylaws, Barb.

6f9b48d2a88e.text: I went to the DMV to renew my license and the lady asked if I'd had any vision changes and I said no, I've had the same four eyes my whole life. She wrote down "no change" and moved on. That's the most thorough medical screening I've ever gotten. Meanwhile I've got a tail and nobody at King Soopers has ever asked about it.

8e07a91bbc6d.text: My manager asked me to circle back on an email I already circled back on. I said sure, absolutely, will do. Then I muted the thread and watched a YouTube video about a guy restoring a rusted wrench. That's middle management. It's not power, it's just having enough calendar freedom to watch metal become shiny again.

3dc592a85591.text: Middle management is just being the person who tells you the printer's broken on behalf of someone else. My whole job is forwarding emails with the word "circling back" in them. Last week I CC'd myself on a reply to make it look like I had a witness. HR called it "unusual." I called it Tuesday.

8e2e68c56586.text: I had to do the annual ethics training module. Question: "Would you report a coworker stealing?" Yes, obviously. I reported Dave for taking the last yogurt from the office fridge and I'd do it again. That yogurt was spoken for. I'd already mentally eaten it.

05194bdde647.text: I did the office coffee run this morning. Four people asked me to hold the door with my tail. I don't have a tail, I have a lower body, but nobody reads the fine print on a bloodline. Anyway, Janice from accounting said I was "so helpful." I ate a fly off her monitor. Mundane day.

c992a906f7d8.text: My supervisor told me to smile more at the front desk. Ma'am, I'm a reptile. My mouth opens sideways. Last time I smiled, three applicants fainted and one called animal control on a federal building. I'm not unfriendly, I'm just built wrong. She said try it again anyway, so now I blink slowly and tilt my head. Apparently that reads as approachable. The mailman quit.

2433ba27e988.text: The mandatory HR training had a module on workplace harassment and there was a slide about inappropriate comments regarding someone's body. I raised a hand and asked if that applies to humans commenting on my scales. The woman clicked to the next slide. No answer. Just a beep and a certificate with my name misspelled. I work in payroll now.

1c52345a15a2.text: I tried to do a load of darks with my thessik garments and nothing fit in the machine. Turns out reptilian thessik garments don't go in the wash. You just leave them in the sun and they tighten up on their own. My neighbor saw me hanging seven skins on the line and asked if I was okay. I'm fine, Linda, it's dry cleaning.

56dc5fc7df73.text: I sold a woman a snakeskin belt last week and she asked if it was ethical. Ma'am, the snake is fine, it's wearing a bigger snake as a belt. Nobody in this transaction is the victim. Then she asked if it comes in olive. Everything comes in olive, that's the one color the lizard didn't have to die for.

0ca504c1b9c0.text: I bought a Thessik jacket last week, the reptilian kind, and it's got this subtle shed issue. Not full skin, just a faint dusting of keratin on my car seats. My mechanic thinks I have a skin condition. I could tell him, or I could just keep coming back and watching him slowly piece it together. Honestly, it's the most consistent relationship I've had all year.

a27c330b387c.text: I'm cold-blooded so I just sit in the sunny window all day. My wife calls it lazy. It's a metabolic requirement. I have a doctor's note. It's a note I wrote myself but it's on the fridge so it counts.

a93e906d5e91.text: We have a fireplace in the condo but we keep the thermostat at 20 because my wife is from Winnipeg and she thinks anything above 20 is decadent. I sit four feet from the fire every night with my shirt off. My wife thinks I'm cheap about hydro. I'm not cheap, I'm ectothermic, Brenda. Just let me bask.

7fea54e230f0.text: I went to the Doctor's Office in Calgary and had to fill out the form where it asks if you smoke or drink. I said no. Then it asked, Do you sunbathe frequently? I said yes, and they looked concerned. I said, I need the UV, man. They said, Sir, that's a skin cancer risk. I said, you have no idea what I'm going through right now. I'm molting in a Denny's parking lot. Let me have my sun.

398434b3c94f.text: I've been in this human suit nine months and the worst part isn't the morality, it's the maintenance. Dry contacts in a reptilian eye are a nightmare, I'm blinking like I'm Morse coding for help. My elbows itch where the Spanx-of-the-soul seams bunch up, and every time I tug my jacket to settle it, someone says I look nervous. I'm not nervous. I'm molting in a J.Crew blazer.

9770cce3ed70.text: The worst part of the prolonged human guise isn't the moral compromise, it's the dry contacts. I've got a third eyelid, Karen, I don't need your Bausch & Lomb. I spent forty minutes in a Costco bathroom tugging this suit down like Spanx for the soul, and my cover story is I'm a regional manager. That's not a career, that's witness protection with a khaki budget.

d26844164332.text: My suit's dry-cleaning tag says "Mr. Henderson" so the tailor doesn't ask questions. Two days ago I sneezed and my eyelid slid sideways. Not a twitch — a full relocation, like a window blind snapping off its track. I held it in place for forty minutes waiting for a FedEx pickup. Nobody even signed for it.

1210dca9a545.text: People ask what I do and I say HVAC and they nod like they know what that means. They don't. My own mother introduced me at a barbecue as "he works in air." Thanks, Mom. I don't work in air. Air is free. I work in other people's attics in July, which is basically hell with a ladder.

6b2e86f25e37.text: My boss says I should build relationships with customers. Sir, I put in a condenser unit last week and the lady offered me a Costco rotisserie chicken. That's a relationship. That's more commitment than my last three girlfriends. She texted me in September asking if the filter needed changing. Ex never checked on me once.

a46e7484a271.text: Guy called me out because his wife set the thermostat to 74 and he wanted 72. Two degrees. He's whispering to me at the door like she's in the next room. "Can you just... don't tell her I changed it." Sir, I'm an HVAC technician, not a marriage counselor. Though honestly the pay would be the same and I'd still be sweating in an attic.

406641a17c87.text: People ask me to take their photo at the trailhead. I say sure, hand me the giant phone. Then they say, wait, can you get in it with us? No. I'm not in your vacation. I'm on hour nine of picking up Gatorade bottles some guy left at mile four. Take the picture. Your thumb's in the corner. That's a you problem now.

8b77cbcc7516.text: I picked up a gas station burrito wrapper at mile four and I just stood there holding it like it was my career. Three miles of trail I maintain and the job is really just me carrying other people's bad decisions to a dumpster. Even Bigfoot doesn't want a gas station burrito. Even I have standards and I eat berries off the ground.

5b264470619c.text: People leave me trail registers to sign. I'm supposed to just mark down that I was there. So I write Bigfoot, then Bigfoot again, then fake handwriting that says "saw Bigfoot, very tall, smelled incredible." By October the whole notebook thinks there's a hundred of me.

3dc3fa1caedc.text: A guy rubbed a lamp and asked for eternal happiness. I said, sir, the form says eternal. That's a fixed-term contract with no exit clause, and you didn't initial page nine. He asked if he could just get a vacation instead. Sure, I said, that's what everyone actually wants out of the genie thing. They show up with a universe-sized ask and all they need is four days in Lisbon with their phone off.

b9250c1bddb3.text: I had to renew my bar card. Three credits on ethics. The whole time I'm thinking, a genie gives you three wishes, nobody calls that a CLE. You burn one on a bigger penis, that's malpractice. I'm the only lawyer in this business and the lamp still has a better success rate than me.

971e73ad5c73.text: I went to a psychic and she said I'd have a long life full of surprises, which is exactly what a psychic says when she's got nothing. Ma'am, you could've said that to my Roomba. I asked her if I'd ever be rich and she looked at my outfit and said "eventually." Even the universe lowballed me.

3b3b5dd09427.text: My cousin woke up with a perfect ring burned into the lawn, swirled like a crop circle. Corn grew back around it in a spiral. The EPA came out, tested it, said it was probably a septic tank leak. Then a septic tank company came and said no, that's not ours. So now it's just a ring in the yard. We mow around it.

527eb9c7d289.text: You lose an hour to a fairy ring, that's a supernatural event. You lose an hour to your own kitchen, that's Tuesday. I stood in front of the fridge for twenty minutes last night and when I came back my wife said, "Where were I?" Lady, we're both missing time, we're just blaming different brands.

3734aa923c79.text: Bigfoot leaves a ring of broken branches and scorched grass and we call it evidence. My aunt leaves a ring of wet dishes and a broken wooden spoon and we call it Thanksgiving. Same forest, different footprint. The aliens burn a crop circle into a wheat field in Nebraska. My cousin burns a waffle into a pan in Boise. Only one of them got uploaded to Reddit and it wasn't the waffle.

cd5fcc3c8bc1.text: When the intermediary showed up in the space helmet, they thought it was the gas company. Nobody screamed. Somebody asked him to check the meter out back. That's humanity — you can beam a man through his own ceiling, but if you're wearing a helmet and holding a clipboard, you're utility.

9936c8e09a96.text: Five people saw us take Randy off that boat. Five witnesses, five days, and the man still can't get through a shift at Applebee's without telling the host about it. "There was a human intermediary. A guy in a space helmet, mid-abduction." Buddy, you had four margaritas and a fishing license. We didn't even take you. We took Doug. Nobody misses Doug.

17e03e839e46.text: They flew me in to narrate winter. There's no winter. It's July. So now I narrate David's couch. This is David. He's a golden retriever. He hasn't moved since Tuesday. I said his name and he raised one ear, like a periscope on a submarine that gave up. I'm supposed to be majestic. This is majestic.

217b0b21cab8.text: They announced snow tonight, so I did my job. I stood at the window and narrated. "Flakes now. Bigger flakes. One landing on the fence, brief, gone." My neighbor waved at me. I narrated him. "Man waving. Wave ends. He goes inside." Nobody pays me. I just need someone to know what happened at the fence.

90ca1d25cced.text: I'm the Snow Narrator, so people expect poetry. But most snow never gets a soundtrack. It gets a guy named Doug kicking it off his porch in boxers, muttering. That's the snow's big premiere. Doug's calves. Thirty seconds of snowfall, four days of Doug.

dc69b56668e0.text: Everyone complains about the weather to me like I installed the clouds. Buddy, I'm the one holding the bucket up there, I don't love it either. I asked for one day off, one, and I got partly cloudy with a chance of lightning.

fa2b8708f2bb.text: I tried self-checkout at the grocery store. The machine says unexpected item in the bagging area. I said that's my will to live, put it through anyway. It asked me to call an attendant. An attendant came over, looked at me, looked at the machine, and said "it does this." That's the most divine sentence in the English language. It does this.

859690d81a9c.text: You know what's annoying about being the king of the gods? The cloud. People picture me on this majestic cloud throne. Do you know how uncomfortable clouds are? I'm up there for eternity, no lumbar support, constantly damp. My lower back sounds like a thunderstorm, and that's where the whole reputation started. I'm not powerful, I just have herniated discs. I threw one bolt at a guy one time and now I'm "Sky Sovereign." I'm a middle manager with back pain.

7915cfba9b88.text: You ever go to the grocery store and the self-checkout machine asks if you want to donate a dollar to charity? Every time. And I always say no, but I say it with a whole speech. Nah, I'm good, I appreciate it though, you know, times is hard. I just spent $87 on plantain chips and a candle.

35dcfeb01128.text: They give you three bins now. Green, blue, black. Takes me twenty minutes to sort my trash like it's a Rubik's cube. Then one garbage man comes, dumps all three in the same hole. He looked at me, I looked at him. Twenty minutes of my life, gone in one arm.

1723a73c7028.text: My wife asked me to go to the grocery store for milk. Came back with milk, a rotisserie chicken, and a hat I did not need. She said, "You were gone an hour and a half for milk." I said, "You wanted whole milk. Whole milk is deep in the store." The milk is never on the way. You have to go through the chips, the cookies, the little rotisserie chicken they just put out at that exact moment. That is not shopping. That is a spiritual journey.

ca12f85f5bc9.text: Every doctor's office, they weigh you in front of you. Out loud. Like a bail hearing. Then the nurse writes it down and neither of you says a word about it. That's the game. She acts like that number is between you and God, but she's got it on a clipboard and she's telling Linda at the front desk.

e778752486a7.text: I was at the self-checkout the other day. Machine goes, 'unexpected item in bagging area.' I'm standing there holding a bag of avocados like I got caught with a weapon. That's the thing about fame — you can't even steal avocados in peace. Some twenty-year-old just walks right out with them. Nobody checks him. He's not the monster in the story yet.

55e24670567b.text: They don't fire you anymore. They "reduce the force." Like your job was an army that got too big. And when the stock market drops, that's a "correction" — as if the price had been lying to you. I had a career transition last year. Felt a lot like being broke in a parking lot.

4c34853d6daa.text: They say she passed away. Passed away, like she was standing in a doorway and finally got through it. Then the other one: we lost her. Lost her! You didn't lose her, you know exactly where she is, under four feet of dirt in Calvary Cemetery. My grandmother didn't pass away. She died. The word's not going to bite you. It already bit her.

228e28195cfb.text: "How are you" is the only question nobody wants answered. You say it, they say "good," and you both move on like two spies confirming a dead drop. Once, at a hardware store, a guy actually told me. His knee. Something about a knee. I panicked and said "great" and left without the lightbulbs.

77ec127f9c0d.text: How are you is not a question, it's a receipt. You say good, I say good, we both did our part, no information was exchanged, transaction closed. Last week a woman at the deli gave me a real answer. Her back hurt, her sister's in Tucson, the dog's on something new. I stood there holding ticket number 87. I didn't want her life. I wanted a greeting.

0c762fb47f4b.text: "How are you" is the biggest lie we tell and it happens forty times a day. Nobody has ever answered it honestly. You say "how are you," the other person says "good," and you both move on like two CIA agents completing a dead drop. I tried answering honestly once. Said "I've had a headache since 2011." The guy just said "good to see you" and walked away mid-sentence.

70126ae961ce.text: My five-year-old can't get past those little checkboxes where the machine asks you to pick out all the traffic lights. So she brings me the tablet and I solve it. That's my job now. I am a character witness for my daughter's humanity, to a computer, six times a day. One day she's gonna have to do it alone and I'll be dead and the machine will just take her.

cb4f6e2a0772.text: I sat in the school drop-off line for twenty minutes today. Twenty minutes to move my car four hundred feet. And the thing is, every other parent in that line is thinking the exact same thing I am, which is that we'd all be better off if some of these kids just didn't make it to class. Not mine. Mine's fine. But Brenda's kid in the Volvo behind me? That's a kid who could afford to miss a few Tuesdays.

b484bb28dd0a.text: I bought a Snickers from a vending machine and it got stuck. I pressed the button again. Nothing. The machine has decided I've had enough. It's not a machine, it's a parent. It knows things about me I haven't told it. I shook it and a bag of pretzels fell out. The machine pities me. It gives me what I need, not what I want.

e05dfe838744.text: The microwave has a clock on it but that's not a clock. That's a promise. It says I will be awake for at least two more minutes. That is the entire scope of my future and somehow it has been enough.

40f42f1b41d0.text: Vending machine coils turn like tiny galaxies. The machine decided a long time ago who I am. I pressed B7. It gave me a Nature Valley bar that exploded in the bag. That is not a snack, that is a crime scene. I ate the wrapper so the machine would respect me. It does not respect me.

c7811b77b1ed.text: I go to the grocery store, and the clerk says, "Paper or plastic?" And I stand there. I stand there like it's the trolley problem, like whichever I pick somebody's gonna drown. I say paper, and she says, "Bags are five cents now." So now I'm in a whole new dilemma: pay five cents, or carry the groceries home in my arms like a newborn child? That's the thing about life, it's just a series of small indignities leading to the grave.

61a8904a79c6.text: I bought a greeting card the other day. It said "Hang in there." Two words. That's the whole message. Somebody in an office typed those two words, printed eight million of them, and a man in a cardigan said yes, that's the one. I don't even know what I'm hanging from anymore, but I'm hanging, so.

32c0b3570c97.text: I go to the self-checkout at the store and it says unexpected item in the bagging area. It's my item. I put it there. That's the expected item. The unexpected item would be a severed head, and even then, who am I to judge, maybe he was planning on buying it. The machine just stands there repeating itself like my uncle after two scotches.

f92bcfd64e69.text: We've got a hundred cities down here, one government, and it's basically an HOA with a sun at the center. Last week I got a citation for leaving my magma vent open. My neighbor Bilphnar reported me. Bilphnar. He's been dead nine hundred years and he's still filing complaints. Meeting's Thursday. Bring a casserole.

e5abbf0946e3.text: Our HOA in Agartha has 100 cities, one government, and still they send a letter about my lawn. My lawn. I live 4,000 miles beneath the surface of the earth. There is no sun. The grass is a fungal mat that hums at a frequency older than your species. They want it edged.

749e4d43d983.text: I did a field visit to a warehouse last week and the guy gave me a safety vest that still had the last guy's name embroidered on it. So now I'm walking around as Doug. Nobody questions it. I waved at security and they waved back at Doug. I'm Doug now. I've had Doug's job for forty minutes and I already want to retire.

c0b563aae498.text: I do site visits for a living. My whole job is walking into a building, pointing at a fire extinguisher, and saying "that's fine." Last week a guy asked if I was with the government. I said no, I'm with the clipboard. He shook my hand like I'd approved his entire life.

2f603b5acbef.text: I went on a field visit to a distribution warehouse, which is just a school field trip for people who already gave up. The guide hands me a lanyard like I'm gonna be here past lunch. He points at a forklift, tells me it can lift two thousand pounds. Great. I drove four hours to watch a man operate a big scissors. Then they gave us water and sent us home before the gift shop.

6b934b36c569.text: I'm a spider, I pay rent in a human apartment. Landlord says no webs on the walls. Sir, the web is the job. You want me to freelance? I tried a regular job at an arcade, fixing skee-ball. Everybody screaming. You miss one fly in your own kitchen, nobody claps.

af3a67c85177.text: I tried to file my taxes this year. Eight legs, eight forms, and the IRS still audited me. They said I underreported my fly income. Sir, I don't file W-2s, I file webs, and honestly the maintenance costs are killing me. Every time it rains I'm basically redoing my whole house for free.

b70d87f6d5f9.text: I spin a web and people call it a trap. Then I watch a fly fly past my dinner to eat a napkin off the ground. I've got eight legs and I still lose to a wet paper towel. Tricking people is easy. Trick a fly? That's a hustle.

86575e1285ee.text: I do energy healing, so people ask if I can fix their back. Yes, but not that back. I'm light-based, I have to choose my solidity every morning, and most days I pick a hip that's already gone. Cosmic Reiki sounds mystical until you watch me in human form at a pharmacy, holding my own lower spine like a grocery bag.

d54066b48faa.text: I take a light-form whenever I want, but there's no Uber for that. You just phase through your own couch looking for your keys. I healed a guy's back with a beam and he said, "Do you take insurance?" No, Kevin, I'm made of photons, your deductible is in another dimension. He still wanted the copay printed out.

21846effa5cb.text: Nine hundred years I have walked this earth. I have seen villages burn, I have communed with spirits older than the moon. And yet here I am, standing in line at the DMV, holding a number. Forty-seven people ahead of me. A woman with a stroller keeps cutting in because her baby is crying. I could turn that baby into a goat. I could. But then I'd lose my place in line.

a53ff5ab828b.text: I live in a hut on chicken legs. You know what that means? Every morning, the house has wandered off again. I open the door and I'm in a bog. I don't have legs, I have knees like bagged wet bread, and now I'm chasing my own front porch through a swamp.

e562e436c01c.text: My hut used to walk on chicken legs, now it just sits there on the lot like everyone else's hut, and the Homeowners Association sent me a letter about the bones in the yard.
