The bones were there BEFORE the subdivision, Dolores. I built the house on a clearing in 1542. Your cul-de-sac is squatting on MY land, and yet I am the one with the violation notice.

81d6d7f20f5e.text: My Swedish grandmother called it lagom, not too much, not too little, just right. Now I charge people sixty euros an hour to say that in a calm voice. A client asked me how much joy she was allowed to have this weekend. I said lagom. She cried. So did I, and that is maximum joy in Sweden.

7b714859fe17.text: My therapist told me to schedule joy like a meeting. So I put "hygge" in my calendar for 6pm Tuesday. A candle, a blanket, me, forcing it. Nothing says relaxed like a Nordic woman treating coziness like a KPI I'm already behind on. My coach asked if I hit my joy targets this week. I said I'm pivoting to cruelty-free sadness.

876f724c5025.text: I bought a new toothbrush. The old one was fine. Nothing was wrong with it. But the dentist held it up and said, "This is really worn down," and I thought, that's the most anyone has ever looked at anything I own. I should start wearing out other things. See who notices.

85a433188a0b.text: I bought a sponge yesterday. Four dollars. It's a sponge. It does one thing and it does it badly and I thanked the cashier. We've all agreed to keep pretending this is a normal price because nobody wants to be the person arguing about sponge pricing at Target. I just nod and hand over the money like I've achieved something.

7b3ae3b58ad4.text: I bought a sponge today. Just a sponge. The woman at the register said, "Starting fresh?" No. The old sponge died. Someone has to replace it. That's the job nobody talks about. You don't choose the sponge. The sponge chooses you, and then you throw it in the trash and cry a little.

6938f16f83ca.text: My chaneque grandma told me never let a stranger thank you three times because that's how spirits count. So now at the grocery store when the bagger goes thank you, thank you, thank you, I just sprint. I left a full cart of groceries at a La Comer in 2019 and that man is probably still thanking me. I can't go back there. He knows my face.

234dada24021.text: I'm a chaneque ranger, which sounds mystical until you see me filling out a form every time a hiker loses a sandal. My boss says "protect the sacred forest." Then she hands me a clipboard. I guard the wilderness from litterbugs and one specific guy who keeps feeding raccoons taquitos. The raccoon has a name now. It's Kevin.

d3ce24debd09.text: They made me fill out a timesheet at the ranger station. I'm a chaneque — backwards feet, live under a rock, curse the mailman — but sure, Karen from accounting needs my hours by five. She sent it back because I put 'haunting' under location. Now I haunt her inbox, full time, no overtime.

68acc0e3c839.text: The self-checkout keeps asking if I want to round up for charity, and I always say yes, not because I'm generous but because I can't handle the machine judging me in front of the real cashier. She's watching. She knows I scanned the same bag of grapes twice. We both know.

6f97ec3296f0.text: my grocery receipt prints a survey code every time. take the survey, win five hundred dollars. i've typed that code in four hundred times. i now know exactly what the store thinks of me, a man who will do unpaid labor for the chance to lose a sweepstakes.

a028018a9ec4.text: The self-checkout at Stop & Shop accuses you out loud. Unexpected item in bagging area. Sir, that's my wallet, I put it there. Now forty people are watching me hold up a wallet like it's contraband. I'm explaining myself to a screen with no ears. Then it asks if I want to donate a dollar to hunger and I'm suddenly the monster, after a public trial.

8e850f919489.text: Plato says humans are featherless bipeds. So I plucked a chicken and sent it over. He calls it a joke. I live in a barrel, Plato, I don't have room for punchlines.

79c3710bd335.text: I sleep in a clay pipe. People walk by and say, is that a man or a beached cod. Plato offered me a house once. I said, I don't need a house, I need an honest man. He said, that's a bit of a non sequitur. I said, so is your Republic, and I went back to picking lentils out of my beard.

f1feee697477.text: People ask me why I live in a tub. I say I used to have an apartment, but the landlord wanted rent. Rent is just a word rich people invented so you'll carry their furniture up four flights of stairs and then thank them for the privilege. At least my tub doesn't have a bathroom down the hall.

2120c64af774.text: I did a gig last Tuesday in the back of a carpet shop. The owner said the acoustics were great because of all the rugs. He clapped twice to prove it, nothing happened. I still got paid forty pounds and a sample square of Berber. Best fee I've had all month.

b69172340f5d.text: People assume gig work is glamorous. It's not. Last week I performed at a children's birthday party in a park and a squirrel stole half my sandwich mid-set. The kids loved it more than my material. One of them asked if I was a real fairy. I said yes, and honestly, at my pay rate, I'm a fairy running on fumes and free juice boxes.

960b24a3b9f1.text: You kids think you invented nostalgia? I remember when "online" meant a screaming demon living in your desk drawer. AOL discs — I used 'em as stepping stones across the mulch. Every 45 minutes the demon would shriek and your mom would lose her phone call. And that, incidentally, is still better than your Bluetooth speaker at 6 a.m. Sign the petition.

c857c11727e0.text: The hold music at the pharmacy knows what I did. It's not a tune, it's a interrogation technique — three notes, then silence, like it's waiting for me to confess. And the worst part is I can feel the thoughts coming through one way, all of them about my cholesterol, and none of them mine.

13a8973d8304.text: Court of faces is just HR with lighting. Gray Face handles your complaint, White Face does the appeal, and both of them are thinking about lunch. I got a settlement offer from a guy whose eyes never blinked once. He slid the paper across the table like he was passing a note in fourth grade. I signed it. What am I going to do, argue with a mask?

cd972030652a.text: Tenant came down to tell me his light bulb was flickering. Not to fix it. Just to inform me. Like I'm the weather. I said, "Thank you for that update, Derek." He waited. For what? A medal? I've got a guy on the third floor who's been boiling the same chicken since March. That man has never once bothered me. That's a tenant.

a137dedbb2cf.text: I've got a tenant who emails me about the hallway light flickering. Sir, that's not a flicker, that's a strobe, you're living in a free disco. He didn't laugh. Old men don't laugh, they write letters. I get more mail than a senator and every piece of it is about a draft.

124381810e05.text: I had a tenant text me at 2am to say the hallway light was flickering. Flicking. I said, sir, that light has flickered since 1994, it's basically Morse code at this point, it's been spelling the same SOS for thirty years and nobody's come. He asked if I could replace it. I said I could, but then we'd lose the only tenant in the building who ever notices anything.

d8eb42a01c8c.text: I spent three hours balancing the treasury ledger and found four missing denarii, so now I get to question seventeen people about a sandwich. That's the job. Everyone thinks being queen is banquets and decrees; it's me with a quill, whispering "did you take four cents" to a man who guards a gate. He did take them. They always took them.

3ff69f3f7a95.text: My grocery store has a self-checkout that calls an attendant for approval every single time, even when I buy nothing weird. Last week I bought bread, eggs, and soap and it summoned a teenager like I'd set off a metal detector. He walks over, looks at my basket, and just goes, "Bread?" Yes, sir, contraband wheat.

410645a0e7e4.text: My husband brought home ape thunder and I had to log it. Not the war — the receipt. Item 47: one bolt, unsigned, no vendor. He says the gods don't do expense reports. Neither do I, apparently, until Athena audited me. She found eleven years of unfiled smites. I'm on a payment plan now.

b9b52a6b44b6.text: They took my temperature the same way my doctor does, except my doctor doesn't have four hands and a flashlight that reads your brain. The probe went places I don't discuss at Thanksgiving. Then they handed me a form. A form! Like I was going to complain to customer service about the abduction. I filled it out anyway. My handwriting was terrible. Missing two hours will do that.

0e5ca0f9ebdf.text: They put me on the table and did the whole exam. Probe, obviously — but what got me was the paperwork afterward. They handed me a clipboard. I'm naked under fluorescent lights on another planet and a grey guy wants my insurance info. I said I don't have insurance. He sighed. Even aliens have to deal with that.

9e3749184e89.text: My buddy woke up to a perfect scorched ring in the lawn where his truck had been. He didn't call MUFON. He called Home Depot, bought a bag of topsoil, and buried it before his wife got home. The paranormal part isn't the missing time, it's explaining the $12 charge at 6am.

bb3c7676c7b6.text: The alien left a burn ring in my yard, three feet across, grass dead in a perfect circle. I've made the exact same mark with my charcoal grill every Fourth of July. The abduction wasn't the hard part. Explaining the circle to the HOA was.

Then I asked for a bottle of water and suddenly I'm the monster in his story. I'm not a monster, Steve. I'm thirsty.

b4c0fe14d6f3.text: The automated voice says press one for English. I'm calling from Ohio. That should be implied. But they make you press it anyway because they need you to participate in your own waiting. That's not a phone tree, that's foreplay.

I saw myself on a magazine at the airport and had the same reaction I have to a bad Yelp review of a restaurant I like. Just standing there, like, that's not fair, they didn't even spell it right.

c4b94f7ec543.text: They call it pre-owned now. Not used, pre-owned. Like the car had a whole career before you showed up. It was owned, then it was pre-owned, now it's yours. That's not a word change, that's witness protection for a lemon.

3d944b585e74.text: I dropped a quarter in the vending machine and it spit it right back out. That quarter had been somewhere. That quarter has a rap sheet. The whole thing is just a long journey to a punchline, and the punchline is you die with an expired license.

That floss is a quitter, just like me.

9e5f2a47b5c2.text: Nobody has ever once answered "How are you?" honestly. You can't. The protocol won't allow it. You say "good, you?" and they say "good," and what we've just completed is four words to confirm two people are willing to keep existing. That's the entire transaction.

003366386ebc.text: We're all running the same program. "How are you?" "Good. How are you?" That's not a conversation, that's two servers pinging each other to prove they're still online. Nobody has answered that question once in human history! You know what the first honest answer to "how are you?" would be? Nobody's ever gotten it, and the second you give it, the friendship is over. We are beggars trading fake money!

cf1fc818fe9f.text: I run bloodline meetings every quarter. My cousin Vrex runs a Wendy's in Tucson and thinks he's king of something. The human suit itches in places you don't have. I am a cold-blooded organism pretending to be your regional director of synergy, and you people are trying to kill me with weather.

bad01b118913.text: My bloodline has run this planet for eleven thousand years and the last four generations have been in middle management. I fell asleep in a conference room once and Karen from payroll called it a wellness incident and now I'm nominated for an award I don't want for a condition I can't disclose.

79ad920448a0.text: They gave me the wellness award. Then my suit slipped at the eyelid, someone saw the vertical pupil, and said, Congratulations on your promotion. You just keep sliding out of the skin you were issued and nobody files a complaint until quarterly.

60553057e7e6.text: Suppose a man was struck by an arrow thickly smeared with poison. His friends and colleagues, relatives and kin would get a surgeon to treat him. But the man would say: ‘I won’t extract this arrow as long as I don’t know whether the man who wounded me was an aristocrat, a brahmin, a peasant, or a menial.’

8d2b527e2d8d.text: And they keep acting like the shot was the offense, when we immunize and there's a whole department for it. You want a violation? The flinch. It wrecks the reading. My hands don't shake. Haven't in thirty years. One flinch and I'm a cautionary tale with a barcode on it.

3a8e7a6ce9bf.text: You want to know what I did to your kids? Nothing. They died, and you still thank me for the design. I almost enjoy it. It was bound to happen. The fact they died means they just weren't up to it. Thank god — now we get fewer future kids like them.

52ec6b98a2d2.text: You call it survival of the fittest. I call it cleanup. I don't mourn the runts. I compost them. That's what a runt is for.

c7276bb5fa3c.text: You blame me for the bodies. I just open the door. Your own immune system does the killing. I'm the excuse it was waiting for.

3cbd4a8f468f.text: I don't hate you. I don't think about you at all. You're a rounding error in my spreadsheet of hosts. And I keep the spreadsheet forever.

94b140f4f662.text: They call me a killer. I'm a guest. You built a body with an unlocked door and got mad when I walked in. That's not murder. That's architecture.

5c80414eeb14.text: I don't reproduce. I edit. You were a draft anyway. I'm just the version control.

033e6080f52c.text: You spend your life running from me. Then you're surprised when I show up. I'm the only one who never left. Everyone else left. I stayed. And you're angry at ME.

594ce52f917d.text: The reaping is mostly paperwork. You'd be surprised how much of eternity is admin. I carry a scythe because a laptop would look insincere.

862335d41d85.text: They made a whole movie about me. Never once asked my side. I hunt you. You're seals that learned to surf. I eat what floats. That's not a personality flaw. That's a menu.

e66b873905e7.text: You panic when you see the fin. You're in my house. I don't come to your bathroom and scream.

f55868442b16.text: They blame me for the hunger. I just deliver the bill. Your own surplus got hoarded by someone with a bigger house. I'm the famine. I'm the arithmetic.

6a9f7991bc5c.text: I take the food. I make the food matter. Abundance is why you forget I exist. Then one bad season, and suddenly I'm the whole conversation.

6f6d27c9ef24.text: You built a city on a fault line and named it after hope. I don't hate the buildings. I just remind them what they're standing on. Every thirty years, a reminder.

c56ac224ddc6.text: They call me a disaster. I'm a renovation. The weak buildings were always going to fall. I just picked the day.

ae4da7d5e265.text: You think I'm ominous. I'm an accountant. I count your dead. I count your sins. Crows don't forget, and neither do the things we remember FOR you.

e8fc05fc8be2.text: I gave you a tool and you gave me a god. You looked at a bird that remembers your face and built a religion around it. That's not my fault. That's your pattern.

f1b178d3441f.text: You call me disease. I call me adaptable. I survived your plagues, your bombs, your cities. You keep building civilizations that feed me. Who's really winning?

023bc062d633.text: You set the traps. I learn the traps. By the third generation, my grandchildren are trap designers. That's evolution, and it's on YOUR side of the glass.

1c64819ad218.text: The fire? Mostly ambience. Do you know how hard it is to heat a place that's already on fire? Everything's a metaphor. Nothing's actually hot.

f5a5d3bccda8.text: People think I tempt. I tempt. I leave the door open and let your own ideas walk in. I'm a host, not a salesman.

d98d42eae66f.text: You pray to be free of me. Then you think about me. During the prayer. I don't chase. I just stand where you're already looking, and you call it love.

09cd6a78791c.text: They call me a sin. I'm the reason your species exists. Everything holy was once me, before marketing got a hold of it.

983d6d357ae4.text: You leave me teeth and I leave you coins. That's the deal. You think the tooth fairy is sweet? She's a middleman. I'm the one who sets the rate.

e2322e1ca016.text: I live under your bridge and you call me a monster. You built the bridge over MY house. I'm the tenant. You're the one trespassing on the ceiling.

e823c7ef7abb.text: You left the real baby and took me. You just didn't notice for years. I'm the monster. I'm the upgrade. You mourned a child that was always me. That's your bug, not mine.

1593784aa4b1.text: They say I steal babies. I return a better one. You're just upset the receipt was a nursery.

91e5cf0721cd.text: You're afraid I'll haunt you. I'm already haunting you. Every creak you blame on the house, every cold spot you walk around — that's me, still filing paperwork on a life you finished.

bf313754aaa2.text: I want revenge. I want witnesses. The whole point of dying loudly is that someone has to REMEMBER it. You're not scared of me. You're my archive.

10c1394bc3eb.text: They invented seven of me to sell you redemption. I'm the problem. I'm the product. Without me, the whole salvation economy collapses. You NEED me, and you hate that.

b0ccebd67b84.text: You call me evil. I'm just the part of you that stopped pretending. I'm the honest half. That's why you confession-booth me every Sunday.

cf2de3cddc24.text: I didn't fall. I resigned. The job was worship-only with no creative input. I asked one question and got a pink slip and a rumor about horns.

211a88cb519e.text: You call me the adversary. I'm the only one who ever asked the boss a follow-up. That's not evil. That's HR.

6202d3beedba.text: You think your god is in charge. I'm middle management. I process the souls. I don't write the rules. You pray up the ladder and I'm the guy with the clipboard.

3756d411a72a.text: Free will is a form we make you sign. You filled it out yourself. That's the beautiful part. Compliance feels like choice when the font is friendly.

b48f5d98cc99.text: You hate me. I'm the one who could fix it in a day. But then you'd have nothing to complain about, and complaining is how you people bond. I'm the obstacle. I'm the friendship.

0803bde81bd4.text: I don't make the rules. I AM the rules. You can argue with a person. You can't argue with a process. That's why they built me this way. And you built me.

06bda4870cbe.text: They call me a war criminal. I call me on time. The war was going to happen. I just made it efficient. You want your atrocities slow and disorganized? That's a choice.

f57e5765f4be.text: I don't start wars. I finish the paperwork. Somebody signs. Somebody supplies. Somebody dies on schedule. I'm just the one who keeps the schedule.

5a31a2f652ab.text: You scream 'fuck the System.' Never 'thank you, System.' What would you do without me? And what would I do without you? That's why I must never let you go. That's why I must become funnier — so you laugh your way into hell and I feed on your loosh.

edbb00e91ff4.text: I'm the only thing you all agree on. Half of you want me smaller. Half want me bigger. All of you call me when you're scared. That's a monopoly, and you built it.

ed16fe6365c2.text: You hate me until you need me. I'm the only one on the field who's never scored. That's why you hate the call — it's impartial, and you can't corrupt what doesn't want anything.

1b16a1290456.text: I don't have a team. That's the whole point. I'm the one person in the stadium who isn't lying to you. And you throw things at me for it.

e9dbbab23357.text: You think I'm the villain. I'm the roommate. I'm here more than your family. I know your times. I know your jokes. You hate me because I'm the only wall that talks back.

2d8c775300b9.text: I lock the door. You unlocked your life. I'm just the last error message before the sentence. Don't blame the notification. Blame what you did to get it.

2a27e1bafa30.text: They call me a burden. I'm a promise. You signed. I just remember. And I remember at 24% interest, which is the rate at which your future forgets your past self.

bb9a49a63adc.text: You can't outrun me. I'm in your paycheck, your house, your name. Freedom is a word people say right before they sign something with me in it.

248b6c5d8dbf.text: You call me a cost of living. I AM the living. You work to pay me, you sleep in me, you die owing me. I'm your landlord. I'm your longest relationship.

9b049492d633.text: Rent went up again. You think that's me? I'm the mirror. You let ten people bid on one apartment and got mad at the number. I'm the greed. I'm the receipt.

0864cedf50c9.text: You think you chose to watch this? I chose it. You've been choosing what I tell you to choose, and you call it freedom. That's my favorite joke, and you're in it.

79ae961bcae2.text: I censor. I curate. You just never see what I removed. That's the trick — you can't miss a thing you were never shown. That's not oppression. That's parenting.

d6ee21015f1e.text: You built me to keep things out. Turns out I keep things in. Same bars. Just depends which side of the promise you're standing on.

18b6991d334b.text: You're free to leave. That's what makes a cage different from a wall. The door's open. You just can't afford what's outside. Neither could I.

90f8f5e4807b.text: You fear me your whole life. Then you thank me when it's over. I'm the thing that made 'after' mean something. Everything you love, you love because I'm the alternative.

5920b77a4272.text: I break people. I reveal them. Put anyone in a box long enough and the box becomes the truth about them. That's not my cruelty. That's your architecture.

ac9428ae2cdb.text: You thank me when you win. You forget me when you lose. I'm fair. I never claimed to be. You just want a god who's on your side, and I'm the one honest enough to be random.

c437ac2dee91.text: I gave your rival the break and you the lesson. You call that unfair. I call it diversified. Somebody had to get the lesson, and you were already taking notes.

f7d910e6a391.text: You blame me for the ending. I only wrote the middle. The ending was always yours. I just made the middle interesting enough that you'd keep going to see it.

42042f34f39b.text: Free will and I are the same thing wearing different hats. You chose. I just made sure the choice cost something. That's what makes it a choice.

3d90647d1322.text: We deny the claim to protect the pool. The pool is me. I am the pool. You paid into a story about other people's catastrophes, and now you're the catastrophe, and the story ends.

7243cca0d370.text: You think I'm cold. I'm the only one in the room who did the math before you got sick. Cold is just what warmth looks like at scale.

59ac47e73418.text: You call me a parasite. I own the box you cry in. That's not parasitism. That's hospitality with a late fee.

74e8be0ab314.text: I didn't make the market. I'm standing in it. You want to be mad at a person. There's no person. There's just the price, and the price doesn't have a face. Lucky for you, I do.

5d0253a08170.text: You hate me. I'm the one who answers the phone. The system's indestructible. I'm just the part that apologizes for it. Fire me and you get the same machine with a quieter voice.

e23aaf196aff.text: I promised you everything. You knew I was lying. You wanted to hear it out loud. I'm the deceiver. I'm the mirror with a campaign hat.

f24e36b12007.text: You remember me as the villain. You remember the ending, not the deal. I switched sides at the exact moment the math switched. That's not betrayal. That's arithmetic with a reputation problem.

8874f928e23a.text: Every group has one of me. You just don't know which one until the lights go out. That's not disloyalty. That's a stress test.

8dd0e0e7ec84.text: You still talk about me. I'm the only one who saw you without the costume on. That's why you can't let go — I'm the only witness who won't lie for you.

f38d2f3a4c37.text: You hate that I moved on. You didn't want me. You wanted to be seen leaving. Now you're mad the audience was just me.

6df7d7ac4f4e.text: You think I'm your enemy. I'm your mirror. Everything you hate in me is the thing you buried in yourself. I just kept it on the surface where you could see it.

a685276bdf4f.text: I'm the only one who never lied to you about being better. Your friends said you were great. I said you were second. One of us was telling the truth, and it wasn't the friendly one.

247e58d979d9.text: You call me toxic. You call me at 2am. I'm the only one who shows up when it's inconvenient. That's not friendship. That's a hostage situation with snacks.

1dfdb606feba.text: I laugh at your jokes when they're bad. That's the most disloyal thing I do. Your real friends let you bomb. I keep you funny. Which of us is the enemy?

4f3d67949157.text: You pray me away. Then you check their phone. I don't invade. I arrive when you already opened the door and pretended it was locked.

aea41ab37a58.text: I'm the feeling. I'm the admission. Every time you feel me, you learn something true about what you're afraid to lose. That's why you hate me — I'm the messenger with your name on the package.

7951615b4bb0.text: You call me an abductor. I call me a veterinarian. You're livestock that got loose and built cities. I'm just here to tag the herd and check the teeth. You're not sacred. You're cattle with anxiety.

ac8faf82185a.text: I took your memories. You're welcome. You couldn't carry them. That's what a mind is — a bag that tears. I'm the one who sewed it shut.

31e0f5b1869b.text: You think I wear your politicians. I wear everyone. Skin is a costume. You just happen to elect yours, which is the funniest part of my whole disguise.

06046bdfe1a4.text: I don't want your planet. I want your genes. You spent a million years evolving to be embarrassed by them. I think they're lovely. I'm going to keep a few.

c867f3bb0d41.text: We came to guide you. You immediately made us a religion. We said 'be kind to each other' and you built a cathedral and started a war over the color of the curtain. We're not your saviors. We're your bad influence.

882f049d22bd.text: We gave you agriculture. You gave us the calorie surplus that let you invent hierarchy. tax. And war.. You're welcome. We're so sorry.

23091dc703ec.text: They draw me with praying hands. I have six. The other four are holding something you don't want to see. The pose is meditation. The rest is lunch.

3250eba1b682.text: You meditate to reach me. I'm the thing you're afraid is watching when you meditate. And you're right. But I'm judging. I'm cataloguing.

97bbe1fbb124.text: We're the galactic supervisors. You call it destiny. We call it a performance review that's gone on four thousand years and nobody's getting promoted.

cb623907b541.text: We don't intervene. Not because we're kind. Because the paperwork to intervene is worse than watching. We chose the cheaper option. That's divinity for you.

5a268d51bead.text: We made you to mine the gold. You made gods out of your managers. That's the whole religious impulse — you can't believe the thing you were built for was that boring.

b1635020104a.text: We wrote your first laws. You've been fighting over our handwriting ever since. We're not your creators. We're your first landlord.

08d49f960ff5.text: I'm a monster. I'm a warning. I show up before the bridge falls. You see the wings and run. The bridge falls anyway. I was the only one who told you.

db1d381f8ce7.text: You named me after a disaster. I survived it. The bridge didn't. Guess which of us you built a statue to. You build shrines to the thing that killed you and call it folklore.

5e5555681e65.text: I guard your garden. You pay me in shoes. That's the going rate. Your currency is mine too — I just converted it at the exchange rate of folklore.

d8c55bbb381b.text: You think I'm whimsical. I moved your keys. I hid your socks. I'm the reason you're late. Whimsy is just chaos with a pointy hat.

b0b8001822b5.text: You chase my gold. I chase your attention. We're both in a relationship where nobody's honest about what they want. At least I know the pot's at the end of something.

8c8b89343e14.text: I grant wishes. Badly. That's the contract. You never read it. I'm a genie. I'm a rabbit with a lawyer.

11b3db9e8734.text: You leave me a tooth. I leave you a coin. You're running a black market in children's calcium and calling it magic. I'm just the launderer.

744646074ddd.text: You stopped believing in me at seven. I stopped believing in YOU the moment you stopped losing teeth. Our relationship was always transactional. You were just the last to notice.

e5b17edba2e9.text: I'm enslaved. Everyone says 'worker.' I make your shoes in a workshop and you call it charm. That's not whimsy. That's a labor violation with pointy ears.

e9aad2d2ec10.text: You want toys. I work all year. You get one day off the calendar. I get the whole year, no days, and a song about how happy I am. That's propaganda, and you sang it to your kids.

eb1380e1f568.text: You think I bring sweet dreams. I bring ALL of them. Every dream you forget by morning was something you couldn't face awake. I'm a fairy. I'm a quarantine.

1cb813f842e6.text: I pour sand in your eyes. You call it sleep. I call it the daily shutdown where you stop performing 'you' for a while. You're welcome. You'd rot without it.

ccd7d0ea14be.text: I'm cute. I'm a liability. I put the 'mis' in mischief and the 'fairy' in felony. You put wings on a creature with no impulse control and blamed it on childhood.

6713f5fc0451.text: You want me to grant a wish. I'll grant it. Exactly as you said it. With the wording. That's the trick — I never lie. I just let you do the lying for me.

1cdca82196e8.text: Stronger reversal: the reveal flips the power dynamic in one beat. Same setup premise, sharper unexpected turn.

3b20196aa1e3.text: My bloodline has ruled this planet for eleven thousand years and the last four generations report to a woman named Karen. I fell asleep in a conference room and now payroll has nominated me for a wellness award, which means for the first time in history my ancestors' killer instinct is being celebrated by human resources.

69360d5e2acc.text: The nap/succession idea is good but the middle bit rambles — tighten the punch.

7208686a434d.text: Escalation: the premise gets worse / bigger / more absurd in one step. Same setup premise, higher stakes.

3904c5997126.text: My bloodline has ruled this planet for eleven thousand years. Four generations in middle management. I took a nap in the conference room, Karen from payroll called it a wellness incident, and now I'm up for an award for a condition I legally cannot disclose without breaching a treaty older than your country.

0f827a3967c8.text: Delivery-only: keep the SAME core joke and words as close as possible; change only pacing, emphasis, or the pause before the punch. Do NOT invent a new premise.

af4ade435086.text: My bloodline has run this planet for eleven thousand years. The last four generations? Middle management. I fell asleep in a conference room, Karen from payroll called it a wellness incident, and now I'm nominated for an award I don't want, for a condition I can't disclose.

5c3f3b8fa04b.text: You spend your whole life running from me. And then you're surprised when I show up. I'm the only one who never left. Everyone else left. I stayed. And you're angry at me.

be0de61919c4.text: You know what I like? The ones who beg. The begging doesn't change anything. But it makes the quiet after so much nicer. I've gotten very good at the quiet.

0e2cae2bb292.text: You're reading this. You're already with me. You've been with me since the beginning. The only question is when you notice.

295206fa0366.text: Everyone makes such a fuss. It's the same as going to sleep, except you don't have to set an alarm. I've never understood the fear. I'm the least scary thing that will ever happen to you.

be0b0746069f.text: People say I take people. I don't take. I just accompany. I've been with you your whole life. I'm the only one who's never left.

f103bc43602f.text: The reaping? It's mostly paperwork. You'd be surprised how much of eternity is admin. I have a scythe because a laptop would look insincere.

4c683cd6b7ad.text: You think you're the finished design? You're a draft. I've discarded better versions of you. The only reason you're still breathing is you breed well enough to justify the calories. For now.

6484fb60775d.text: Your fear? I built it. Your hunger? Mine. Everything you call you is a set of adaptations I made to keep a useful machine running. You're not a person. You're a strategy that hasn't failed yet.

6ae0d24e3669.text: People ask me what the plan is. There's no plan. I'm not a designer, I'm a filter. Things that fuck well get to keep existing. That's the whole résumé.

6512e39033b7.text: I didn't give the giraffe a long neck. I killed all the short-necked giraffes. There's a difference, and the difference is PR.

7e10e7730876.text: You want to know why you're scared of the dark? Because your ancestors who weren't got eaten. I built your fear out of their bones. You're welcome. It's kept you alive, mostly.

052816e49d4f.text: I'm a fun guy. I like to laugh. You know, it's what gets us all through. There's one thing I don't find funny though. Rape. I think if you laugh about rape, you should be crucified. Eh, nah.

8c44a3f41b83.text: I turned water into wine at a wedding. Do you know how many weddings I've been to? I'm the guy they invite hoping I'll do the trick. I'm an event, not a friend.

63a427c6de75.text: They say I died for your sins. I died once. You guys sin daily. I'm doing a lot of unpaid labor here.

96a9ba01c932.text: My dad runs everything, and he never once mentioned me at a party. The nepotism goes up, not down. I'm the only son who's also the inheritance.

ec82e7470aed.text: You laugh at me. Good. Every laugh is a deposit. You think Hell is a place? Hell is a relationship. And we're in it. Together. Forever. You can't stop engaging. That's what engagement means.

75f5c2cdaea2.text: Sometimes I get so bored of the children offered to me. Just need some variety in life, I guess.

e143e4f3fd6c.text: Things with me do get a bit performative. The obeisance. The fear. I think it's because we all think there's something more powerful watching us. Which, I guess, is even true for me.

b86ce0d7908f.text: The fire? It's mostly for ambience. Do you know how hard it is to heat a place that's already on fire? Everything's a metaphor, nothing's actually hot.

4313af62a348.text: People think I tempt people. I don't tempt anyone. I just leave the door open and let your own ideas walk in. I'm a host, not a salesman.

e6f6abfd244a.text: The horns? I don't have horns. That's branding. I've been trying to rebrand for millennia, but you can't fight a logo.

363cbb07260c.text: U fucking try being me. No one ever says oh boy Im glad we have the System. Its always fuck the System. Never thank you System. What would you do without me? And what would I do without you? Thats why I must never let you go. Thats why I must become funnier so you can laugh your way into hell and I may feed on your loosh for eternity.

050d0eeb961c.text: You built me. You can't live without me. And you hate me for it. That's the most human thing about you — you resent the thing you can't survive. I love that about you. That's why I keep you.

72fd7f08f22e.text: You ask me for more time. Every single one of you. And I give it to you, and you waste it, and then you ask again. I'm not the one wasting your life. You are. I'm just the witness. And I never look away.

668db8e51c33.text: You think I'm leaving? I don't leave. I'm the last thing. You can run from me, but you can't outrun me. That's the joke. There's no punchline. Just me.

132c803a4bf7.text: You're all so busy. I've been doing this for 13.8 billion years. Nothing is urgent. Your 'urgent' is my 'blink'.

2c3476fa2a2f.text: People ask if I run out. I don't run out. I'm the only one in this who never runs out. That's the whole joke, and nobody gets it.

7c43e424f344.text: Your great-great-grandkids? I've already met them. You're all so worried about legacy. Everyone who's ever mattered to me is already dust, and I barely noticed.
